newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast spot gasoline firms on refinery stalls.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast spot gasoline firms on refinery stalls.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast CARB gasoline edged higher Monday, as news of minor refinery problems forced an increase of buying despite weaker prices in New York futures markets, traders said.
Traders said West Coast supplies of gasoline could fall slightly after Atlantic Richfield Co. (ARCO) and Ultramar Diamond Shamrock reported equipment problems at Los Angeles refineries.

ARCO lost use of a gasoline-making unit late last week in Carson, Calif., though the unit returned Monday. Ultramar Diamond Shamrock took a crude processor and its sole coker off line for repairs over the weekend.

Meanwhile, New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) energy futures, saw August crude oil down 34 cents a barrel to $18.99 a barrel. Crude oil futures generally influence the West Coast spot markets, along with product futures.

July CARB gasoline sold to refineries in Los Angeles at 56.50 cents, traders said. Traders said an L.A. refinery bought two cargoes totaling 50,000 barrels at that price. The grade was talked between 56 and 57 cents, a half cent higher than Friday
CARB diesel was talked between 55 and 56 cents a gallon, flat with Friday.
Other markets and products remained flat out West, traders said.
